cells.reason: FSANZ Schedule 19 sets inorganic arsenic 1 mg/kg for 'seaweed', in force (compilation F2024C00908), and Schedule 19 expressly exempts seaweed from the rule that dried foods are assessed on the pre-drying food, so the level applies to dried seaweed as sold and matches this as-sold cell without conversion. The cell is a total-arsenic cell fed by an inorganic-arsenic instrument; because tAs is never less than iAs, a tAs ceiling of 1000 guarantees compliance with the anchor, so the read-across is protective and the anchor is the strictest in-force sovereign seaweed-arsenic line on this basis (HK Cap 132V seaweed iAs 1000 concurs but its regulation 3(2)(b) concentration adjustment leaves the dried-seaweed basis unclear; SG 2026 seaweed iAs 2000 and France CSHPF 3000 dry weight are looser). No non-gated total-arsenic row covering dried seaweed is stricter than 1000; the only same-analyte sovereign rows are catch-alls at the same value (SG Tenth Schedule (b)(27) other food 1000, UY RBN solid foods 1000; TH other food 2000) that could be cited as concurring instruments, and the Israeli dried-seaweed tAs 5000 row is superseded. Outside applicability, for the reconciler: marine macroalgae typically carry tens of mg/kg total arsenic dry weight, mostly arsenosugars, so a 1000 tAs ceiling functions as a near-total exclusion of the category; that is a policy question, not a scope defect.
